key_insight: The paper shows that narrowing the performance gap between homogeneous and heterogeneous asynchronous optimization is impossible under common similarity assumptions, and only a stronger combination of interpolation and local PL conditions yields a better time bound.
engineering_relevance: For distributed training systems, this means data-partition heterogeneity can impose real algorithmic limits, so schedule and worker-speed improvements alone may not recover homogeneous-case performance.
method: Proves impossibility results for any randomized algorithm under first- and second-order similarity assumptions
Tests the weak interpolation regime and shows it is still insufficient
Introduces strong interpolation plus local Polyak-Lojasiewicz conditions to derive a new time-complexity bound
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical analysis and proofs of optimal time-complexity bounds and impossibility results, rather than experimental evaluation.
watch_item: The improved bound depends on stronger structural assumptions, so it may not apply to practical workloads with only mild or poorly verified data similarity.
paper_title: Bridging the Gap Between Homogeneous and Heterogeneous Asynchronous Optimization Is Surprisingly Difficult
